event: The yearly Apple Developer membership is not renewed on time, or renews but App Store Connect keeps showing it as expired, and Pexi disappears from the App Store.
trigger: Card declined or changed, Apple ID email change, renewal button missing, or nobody noticing the date; Apple reports renewal sync glitches that last days to weeks.
cost: New downloads stop the day it lapses (Apple: apps 'will no longer be available for download'); no updates or fixes can be submitted; paid-app status needs the Paid Applications Agreement re-accepted. Every day down is lost Plus signups; a stuck renewal has taken developers a week or more.
detect: Apple emails the account holder before and at expiry (assumed, not seen); no calendar reminder or repo note found, so nobody would know if the email is missed
response: 1. Renew by hand the moment the 30-day window opens (Apple allows renewal 30 days before expiry). 2. After renewing, sign in to App Store Connect and accept any Paid Applications Agreement. 3. If it still shows expired after 24 hours, contact Apple Developer Support the same day.
smallest_fix: Put the renewal date on Jamin's calendar with a reminder 30 days and 7 days before, confirm auto-renew is on with a card that does not expire first, and write the date at the top of the store accounts packet.
fix_cost: 10 minutes, no money (99 USD a year is already a known cost)
sources: https://developer.apple.com/help/account/membership/renewal ; https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/786108 ; https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/840728 ; docs/the-store-accounts-packet.md:23 (99 USD per year, recurring; no renewal date or reminder found by grep of docs/)

event: Apple removes Pexi or closes Jamin's developer account with a vague reason (for example 'spam 4.3' or a licence-agreement clause) and an appeal goes unanswered.
trigger: Apple's automated or human review flags the app or account; 2026 forum threads and a 2026-11-09 write-up show indie accounts closed with no named app and 'decision is final'; fake or incentivised reviews and look-alike apps are among reasons developers cite.
cost: Total loss of the iOS business and every subscriber's ability to renew in-app; a second account may be treated as the same developer. Rare but unrecoverable.
detect: Apple email to the account holder (assumed); nobody would know sooner
response: 1. Reply in App Store Connect within a day with facts (what Pexi is, no account, no tracking, no review tricks). 2. Keep copies of the source, privacy pages, listing text and screenshots outside Apple. 3. Tell subscribers nothing until Apple rules, then decide on the web site and a new bundle.
smallest_fix: Write one paragraph that consciously accepts this risk (one Apple account, no other store, no web version of the paywall) and keep an off-Apple copy of listing text, screenshots and the privacy pages so a rebuild is quick. Do not weaken the paywall or the app to reduce it.
sources: https://developer.apple.com/app-store/review/guidelines/ (intro to section 1, 2.3.1, 3.1.2(a), 5.1.2(i) all name removal or expulsion) ; https://mjtsai.com/blog/2026/11/09/developer-accounts-removed/ ; https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/805678 ; https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/850045

event: An App Store update review (or an Apple re-check of the live app) happens while the Mac is down, restarting after a deploy, or the tunnel is down, so the reviewer sees a broken app and rejects it or flags it as not working.
trigger: Reviewers test with the backend; Apple's 2.1 says to 'turn on your back-end service'; the server is one home Mac whose every push to main restarts it for seconds.
cost: A rejected update costs 1 to several days per cycle; Apple's guidelines say apps that 'stop working or offer a degraded experience may be removed from the App Store at any time'. A bug-fix release could sit behind this.
detect: The 30-minute alarm would email Jamin if the server is down at that moment (checked: server-alarm.yml); the rejection itself arrives by Apple email (assumed)
response: 1. Before pressing submit for review, run the phone probe against the live server and wait for a quiet deploy window. 2. Do not push to main while the build is in review. 3. If rejected for a crash or blank screen, reply with the probe output and resubmit the same build.
smallest_fix: Add two lines to the release checklist: run the probe right before submitting, and freeze pushes to main until Apple finishes review. The alarm already covers detection.
sources: https://developer.apple.com/app-store/review/guidelines/ (2.1(a), pre-submission note, section 4 intro) ; .github/workflows/server-alarm.yml:1-20 ; docs/store/listing.md:129 ('Needs its server up')

event: The Mac restarts by itself (macOS update, power cut) and the Pexi server and tunnel stay down because nobody is logged in.
trigger: Automatic macOS updates are ON and 27.2.1 is waiting for a restart; the server is a per-user LaunchAgent that only starts after login; if Jamin turns FileVault on (finding D1) the Mac stops at a disk-password screen after every restart and cannot log in on its own.
cost: Full outage until someone types a password at the Mac; Jamin will be at the AMD internship (from 2027-05-03). The 30-minute alarm only tells him it is down. Every hour down is failed scans and 1-star risk.
detect: The 30-minute server alarm emails Jamin after two failed probes (checked: server-alarm.yml:4-9); whether auto-login is on is not known
response: 1. Decide once: either auto-login (FileVault stays off) or convert the server and tunnel to system daemons that start before login. 2. Do a real reboot test and confirm the probe passes with no login. 3. If FileVault is turned on later, the reboot test must be repeated and a planned-restart method used.
response_exists: no: the plist comment (mac/launchd/com.shin.server.plist:8-18) flags the gap and says it is 'not decided either way'
tried: no: the kill -9 test proves KeepAlive restarts a crashed process, not a Mac reboot
smallest_fix: Reboot the Mac once on purpose while Jamin is not logged in, see whether the probe goes green, and write down the result. Tie the answer to the FileVault decision (D1) so one choice does not break the other.
sources: docs/security-check-mac-2026-11-16.md:65-71 ; mac/launchd/com.shin.server.plist:8-18 ; mac/README.md:88-92 (E12 kill -9 check) ; mac/README.md:118-121 ; https://support.apple.com/en-euro/guide/mac-help/mchlp1158/12.0 (FileVault disables automatic login) ; https://discussions.apple.com/thread/253682124 (headless Mac after power fail)

event: RevenueCat cannot be asked (key revoked or mistyped after a rotation, RevenueCat outage, or the server just restarted) and every paying subscriber is quietly treated as free once the weekly limits are on.
trigger: The server's Plus check catches every error with no log line and answers 'not Plus' when it has no remembered answer; the remembered answers live in memory only, so a restart during a RevenueCat problem forgets all of them.
cost: Plus subscribers (CA$3.99 to CA$29.99) hit the free cap of 10 scans a week while paying; refund requests via Apple, 1-star reviews, churn. Not live today only because production limits are off (finding C1); it starts the day limits go on.
detect: nobody would know: the failure path writes nothing (checked: scan-quota.ts:215-218) and the alarm probe uses a made-up device that is expected to be free
response: 1. Look at the server log for RevenueCat errors. 2. Check the RevenueCat secret key in the dashboard against the Mac's setting. 3. Restart after fixing; entitlement answers refresh within 10 minutes.
smallest_fix: Log one warning line (rate-limited) with the RevenueCat status on every failed lookup, and have the existing alarm fail when more than a handful of lookups failed in the last hour; before turning limits on, test once with a sandbox Plus device and a deliberately wrong key.
sources: app/src/scan-quota.ts:49-51,194-218 ; app/src/scan-quota.ts:153-161 ; docs/security-check/FINDINGS.md:43 (C1) ; https://www.revenuecat.com/docs/customers/customer-info (client cache: only reached by the app, not by Pexi's server lookups)

event: A shopper was charged by Apple but Plus does not unlock, and emails support; support cannot find them because Pexi has no account, name or email.
trigger: RevenueCat community reports: product not attached to the entitlement, receipt never reached RevenueCat after a network drop, stale cache; the usual fix is 'restore purchases', then a manual grant.
cost: A refund request through Apple or a 1-star review per case; with the support inbox unread, each case becomes a public complaint. Size scales with Plus subscribers.
detect: Only if someone reads useshinapp@gmail.com or a review appears; who reads the inbox is unknown
response: 1. Reply with the Restore Purchases steps (You screen, Restore). 2. If that fails, ask for the Apple order number, look it up in the RevenueCat dashboard and give a manual Plus grant. 3. Check the product-to-entitlement link was not the cause.
response_exists: no: the restore button exists (app/public/js/screens/paywall.js:210,426-439) and the store page covers refunds via Apple (docs/store/index.html:38-42), but no support steps for 'paid but locked' were found
smallest_fix: Write a five-line canned reply and the dashboard lookup steps (by Apple order number, since there is no email), assign one person to the inbox, and do one sandbox purchase on a second phone to prove restore works.
sources: app/public/js/screens/paywall.js:205-252,426-439 ; app/public/js/purchases.js:215-220 ; docs/store/index.html:38-42 ; https://community.revenuecat.com/sdks-51/customers-being-charged-but-purchase-does-not-show-up-in-revenuecat-150 ; https://www.revenuecat.com/docs/test-and-launch/errors (STORE_PROBLEM: 'Don't assume the user wasn't charged')

event: A subscriber gets a new phone, or uses an iPad and iPhone on one Apple ID, and Plus follows one device and drops from the other, or does not follow at all.
trigger: Pexi uses the random device id as the RevenueCat user; RevenueCat's default restore moves the purchase to whichever id restores it and 'only one customer at a time can have access'; a new phone without a Keychain restore has a new id.
cost: Complaints and refund requests from paying users; Apple guideline 3.1.2(a) says a subscription must be 'available across all of the user's devices'. Size: a few percent of Plus users in a year (assumed).
detect: Support email or reviews; nothing automatic
response: 1. Ask the user to tap Restore on the device they want. 2. If the restore setting blocked it, change it in the RevenueCat dashboard. 3. Explain the one-device rule on the paywall if that is the chosen design.
smallest_fix: Open the RevenueCat dashboard, read the restore-behaviour setting, and do one sandbox test: buy on phone A, restore on phone B, see what happens on A. Decide whether one device at a time is acceptable and write the decision down.
sources: https://www.revenuecat.com/docs/projects/restore-behavior ; https://developer.apple.com/app-store/review/guidelines/ (3.1.2(a)) ; app/public/js/purchases.js:215-220 ; BRIEF: device id kept in Keychain plus localStorage (assumed from brief; dashboard setting not checked)

event: Cloudflare has an incident or disconnects the tunnel for hours (or ends free service), and every shopper sees Pexi as not working with no explanation.
trigger: Cloudflare's own incidents (2025-11-18 core outage, 2025-12-05, a 2026-05 tunnel connectivity incident in Anchorage), a single cloudflared instance on one Mac, or its terms letting it end free service at its discretion with no SLA.
cost: Full outage regardless of how healthy the Mac is; the app shows 'no connection' style messages (api.js 'offline' failure), so shoppers blame their phone or leave a bad review.
detect: The 30-minute alarm probes the public hostname so it would fire (checked: server-alarm.yml); the cause would not be known without the Cloudflare status page
response: 1. Open the Cloudflare status page, then the tunnel's status (Down, 1033) versus the origin (502). 2. Restart cloudflared; if the Mac is fine and Cloudflare is down, wait. 3. Post nothing to shoppers; accept the wait.
smallest_fix: Write the two-line rule 'error 1033 means the tunnel is down, 502 means the server is down' with the restart commands, and consciously accept the single-tunnel risk in writing (a second connector on another machine is the paid-effort fix, not needed at launch).
sources: https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-tunnel/troubleshoot-tunnels/common-errors (1033 vs 502) ; https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-tunnel/configure-tunnels/tunnel-availability/ ; https://www.cloudflare.com/terms/ (2.6 free services, section 8, section 11 'as is') ; https://www.ilert.com/postmortems/cloudflare-global-outage-nov-2025 ; https://isdown.app/status/cloudflare/incidents/596689-cloudflare-tunnel-connectivity-issues-via-anchorage-anc-from-2026-05-14-to-2026-05-28 ; app/public/js/api.js:818-886

event: Cloudflare's free bot protection starts challenging the phone app (an HTML 403 the app cannot solve) while the GitHub alarm, which looks different to Cloudflare, keeps passing.
trigger: Cloudflare says Bot Fight Mode and challenge actions 'may challenge API or mobile app traffic', a challenge on a non-browser request becomes a 403, and on the free plan Bot Fight Mode cannot be skipped by a rule; a dashboard default or toggle can change it.
cost: Some or all real shoppers get errors from phones on carrier networks while Jamin sees green; found by 1-star reviews. Size unknown until it happens.
detect: nobody would know until reviews: the alarm runs from GitHub's servers with the phone's headers, not from carrier IPs
response: 1. Cloudflare dashboard, Security, Events: look for challenge actions on the relay hostname. 2. Turn off Bot Fight Mode or the offending rule for that hostname. 3. Re-run the phone check from cellular.
response_exists: yes: mac/08-cellular-check.md covers a check from a phone off wifi, but not this setting
tried: no: not found in any report whether the cellular check was run since build 9
smallest_fix: Open the Cloudflare dashboard once, record that Bot Fight Mode and any challenge rule are off for the relay hostname, and run the cellular check from a phone on mobile data after each build.
sources: https://developers.cloudflare.com/bots/get-started/free/ ; https://community.cloudflare.com/t/api-api-403-api-curl-ok/844595 ; mac/README.md:82-87 ; .github/workflows/server-alarm.yml:5-9

event: The Mac's tunnel software, Node or macOS drift out of support or get upgraded without a test, and the server quietly stops working months later.
trigger: Cloudflare supports only cloudflared versions within one year of the latest release and warns of breaking changes; Homebrew does not upgrade on its own; the server uses Node's still-changing built-in SQLite and an upgrade of Node was already flagged as needing a full test run; Jamin is away from May 2027.
cost: An outage on a date nobody chose, or an unpatched tunnel client; fix time 1 to 3 hours each, at the worst moment.
detect: A broken upgrade shows up as an alarm; a silently unsupported version shows nothing
response: 1. Every 6 months upgrade cloudflared by hand and restart. 2. Never run a blanket 'brew upgrade'; upgrade Node only with the app test suite run first. 3. Run the probe after each change.
response_exists: no: mac/README.md:22-33 has the Node test gate for first install only
smallest_fix: Two calendar reminders (6 months): upgrade cloudflared and check Node and macOS notes, each ending with the phone probe. Record the current versions (cloudflared 2026.9.1, Node 26.7.0).
fix_cost: 10 minutes to set up, 30 minutes each time
sources: https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/networks/connectors/cloudflare-tunnel/downloads/ ; mac/README.md:17-19,22-33 ; mac/01-cloudflare-tunnel.md:19-20

event: The outage alarm fires or fails to fire and nobody notices: it is one GitHub email to one person, with no phone push and no second person.
trigger: GitHub scheduled runs 'can be delayed' or dropped under load, notifications go only to the user who last edited the cron line, public repos are switched off after 60 days of no activity, and an email can sit unread overnight or during class or work.
cost: A night-long outage is found by a 1-star review; during the AMD internship the delay grows. Each missed hour is failed scans.
detect: The alarm email itself; there is no second channel and no proof the alarm has been seen to fail and arrive
response: 1. Read the Actions email, open the run, see which probe route failed. 2. Check the tunnel and server on the Mac. 3. Tell Aurik if it is not fixed in an hour.
response_exists: no: the workflow comment describes how to prove it can fail (run it with origin set to https://evil.example), but no record of this being done was found
smallest_fix: Add a free second watcher (an external uptime monitor on the health route with a phone push to both Jamin and Aurik), run the evil.example test once and keep the email, and confirm the GitHub repo is private or has activity.
sources: https://docs.github.com/en/actions/using-workflows/events-that-trigger-workflows (schedule event) ; .github/workflows/server-alarm.yml:1-20 ; https://dev.to/astraedus/my-production-app-was-down-for-24-hours-and-nobody-told-me-3nma (web search snippet only, not read in full)

event: The Mac's disk fills up (three 4 GB catalogue backups, unrotated server logs, growing databases) and writes start failing before anyone looks.
trigger: Disk had 38 GiB free with a worst case of about 29 GiB used by backups on 2026-11-07; a stale 4.14 GB file is still there; the server's output and error logs go to files that no job trims (rotation not found).
cost: Server errors or a crash loop, a corrupt or failed nightly backup, and the weekly price refresh failing; hours of downtime and possible database damage.
detect: Only after something fails: the backup has a free-space check (checked) but nothing watches the live disk and the alarm only sees symptoms
response: 1. Check free space on the Mac. 2. Delete the old catalogue copy and trim logs. 3. Restart the server and run the probe.
smallest_fix: Have the health route or the alarm report free disk and fail below 10 GiB; add log rotation for mac/logs; delete the stale copy on Jamin's word.
sources: docs/launch-gaps-2026-11-06.md:79-86 ; mac/launchd/com.shin.server.plist:44-50 (log files) ; mac/hammer-refresh.sh:48 (free-space check exists only there)

event: The Mac is lost (stolen, dead disk, water) and rebuilding takes days because the secrets, the backup script and the setup notes live only on that Mac.
trigger: The backup script is in the Mac's own home folder, not this repo; the tunnel credential, config.env (API keys, RevenueCat secret) and launchd setup sit on the same disk; the Mac setup doc is mostly 'unrun'; the catalogue copy is on Jamin's PC (assumed still there).
cost: Days of total outage and loss of the tunnel identity; each day is lost Plus revenue and trust. Adds to known findings D1 and D2 (unencrypted, same-disk backups) by covering what is not backed up at all.
detect: Obvious when it happens; no test shows the rebuild would work
response: 1. Get a replacement Mac and follow the Mac setup order. 2. Restore databases from the newest backup copy that is off the dead disk (none exists today). 3. Create a new tunnel and re-point the hostname.
response_exists: no: mac/README.md is the original setup, written 'mostly without a Mac present' and unrun end to end
smallest_fix: One-page recovery note listing what exists only on the Mac, a copy of config.env and the tunnel credential in a password manager, the backup script committed to the repo, and one nightly copy of the small databases to somewhere off the machine (known fix D2).
sources: docs/launch-gaps-2026-11-06.md:84-86 ('Committed in the Mac's ~/bin, not in this repo') ; mac/README.md:1-8,105-126 ; docs/privacy/breach-plan.md:42 ; docs/security-check/FINDINGS.md:49-50 ; https://dev.to/vineethnkrishnan/i-went-on-a-trip-my-mac-mini-stayed-home-and-kept-texting-me-1ejg (search snippet: power-cut fear) ; https://beancount.io/blog/2026/09/24/3-2-1-backup-rule-small-business-ransomware-restore-tests-guide (secondary source: off-site copy and tested restore)

event: The anjiawenda.com domain expires, is lost, or is suspended, and every installed copy of the app stops working with no way to redirect it except a new App Store release.
trigger: The hostname relay.anjiawenda.com is built into the app (the phone probe and docs name it); who owns the registration and when it renews is unknown; the Cloudflare zone is in Jamin's account.
cost: Every installed app dead until a new build passes Apple review (about 1 to several days); all subscribers affected; a lost domain cannot be recovered quickly.
detect: Registrar renewal emails if the account holder reads them; otherwise nobody would know until the day it fails
response: 1. Find the registrar and renew at once. 2. If lost, buy a new domain, point a new tunnel, ship an emergency app update. 3. Keep the old app talking to a redirect if the domain is recovered.
smallest_fix: Find out who holds the domain registration, turn on auto-renew, write the expiry date on Jamin's calendar with a 60-day reminder, and record it in the Mac setup note.
sources: mac/README.md:17-22 (the account's one zone is anjiawenda.com) ; scripts/phone-contract-probe.mjs:39,50 ; docs/readiness/BRIEF.md (registration owner and renewal date unknown) ; https://dev.to/astraedus/my-production-app-was-down-for-24-hours-and-nobody-told-me-3nma (search snippet: watch each platform's shut-down warning)

event: A server change breaks older installed app builds (different web origin, changed route), and there is no way to tell those users to update.
trigger: Capacitor's web origin already changed once (capacitor://localhost on older builds, https://localhost from the next native build); users do not update on a schedule; no minimum-version gate or 'please update' message was found.
cost: The previous origin episode meant 78,168 failed preflights and zero real calls (launch-gaps item 0); a similar break after launch would fail every user on the old build and show only as generic errors.
detect: The alarm probes as capacitor://localhost only by default; the https://localhost origin and old build versions are not probed by the schedule (checked: workflow default)
response: 1. Keep both origins accepted. 2. Before changing a route, check what the oldest live build sends. 3. If a break is unavoidable, ship an update and keep the old behaviour as long as old builds exist.
smallest_fix: Add the https://localhost origin to the scheduled probe, and write a rule in the deploy checklist: never remove a route or origin until the app version report shows no old builds. A forced-update message is a larger fix and optional.
fix_cost: 30 minutes for the probe, hours for a forced-update screen
sources: docs/launch-gaps-2026-11-06.md:25-39 ; native/capacitor.config.json:6-8 ; .github/workflows/server-alarm.yml:21-30 ; app/server.ts:2141-2162 (appVersion is reported)

event: iOS clears the app's web storage (localStorage) and the app forgets the shopper's settings, consent, onboarding or saved items.
trigger: Developers and Apple forum threads report WKWebView localStorage disappearing under storage pressure or after OS changes, and Ionic forums say Apple treats it as temporary; Pexi keeps the device id in the Keychain as well, which survives, but other values may not.
cost: Small per case: onboarding or the AI-estimate agreement shown again, a lost Plus flag until the next purchase check, a lost setting; bad if it silently turns off something the shopper chose. Cost to the paywall: Plus status is remembered locally, and a wipe may show the paywall to a paying user until restore.
detect: nobody would know; support complaints only
response: 1. On a clear, ask the app to re-check RevenueCat at launch and re-read the Keychain. 2. Keep the consent state re-askable, never assumed on. 3. Tell affected users to tap Restore.
response_exists: partial: the app already asks RevenueCat at every launch (docs/security-check/FINDINGS.md:59) and restore exists
smallest_fix: List every value the app keeps only in localStorage (settings, consent, Plus flag, history), and move any that cannot be recomputed to the Keychain or the server; test with Safari's data cleared on a TestFlight phone.
sources: https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/742037 ; https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/770747 ; https://forum.ionicframework.com/t/cordova-capacitor-localstorage-missing/187519 ; app/public/js/lib/persistence.js:6,36-45 ; app/public/js/purchases.js:54-66

event: Apple or a reviewer questions the age rating (4+, all ages) because the catalogue names liquor products, and the rating is changed or an update is held up.
trigger: The questionnaire answer for alcohol is 'None' while the catalogue holds 7,555 BC liquor products; Apple's table maps 'infrequent' alcohol references to 13+ and guideline 2.3.6 says mis-rating 'could trigger an inquiry'; whether a price list counts as a reference is unconfirmed (FINDINGS says so).
cost: An update rejected or a forced rating change to 13+ right after launch, plus questions on the children's-privacy items already open (F2). Jamin has ruled all ages, so the cost is a delay, not a lost sale.
detect: Apple email to the account holder (assumed)
response: 1. Answer Apple within a day with what the catalogue is (barcodes, names, prices; nothing promotes or shows use). 2. If Apple insists, change the answer to 'infrequent' and accept 13+. 3. Check the Quebec and children's points again if the rating changes.
response_exists: no: the questions are listed as open (docs/store/listing.md:100,143) with no pre-decided answer
smallest_fix: Decide now, in writing, what Jamin will do if Apple asks (hold 4+ and argue, or accept 13+), so a reply can go out in minutes; do not change the shipped answer unless he chooses to.
sources: https://developer.apple.com/help/app-store-connect/reference/app-information/age-ratings-values-and-definitions/ ; https://developer.apple.com/app-store/review/guidelines/ (2.3.6) ; docs/store/listing.md:100,138-143 ; docs/launch-gaps-2026-11-06.md:188-190 ; docs/security-check/FINDINGS.md:76-78

event: A well-meaning launch push (friends, family, a group chat, a discount for a review) breaks Apple's rules on review manipulation and puts the whole account at risk.
trigger: Apple's guidelines say manipulating ratings or reviews, including paid, incentivised or fake feedback, can get a developer expelled; a required review for a feature is also barred under 3.1.2(a); launch week is when people are tempted.
cost: Developer account expulsion (see item 2), the whole business.
detect: Apple email, long after the fact; nobody would catch it first
response: 1. Ask for reviews only from real users, with no reward and no pressure. 2. Use Apple's own review prompt only (the app does). 3. Tell Aurik and anyone helping.
response_exists: no: the app's own prompt exists (app/public/js/review-prompt.js) but no written rule for the humans was found
smallest_fix: One sentence for Aurik and any helpers: ask real users, no rewards, no friends posting five-star reviews, and Apple's prompt only.
sources: https://developer.apple.com/app-store/review/guidelines/ (section 3 intro, 3.1.2(a)) ; https://www.revenuecat.com/blog/growth/the-ultimate-guide-to-app-store-rejections/ ; app/public/js/review-prompt.js:1-10,155-157

event: Apple's yearly SDK deadline, a new iOS release, or a bug needs an emergency app build while Jamin is at AMD full time, and only Jamin can sign in to build and upload.
trigger: Apple's 2026 rule already forces Xcode 26 or later (since 2026-04-28), a similar rule is likely each spring (assumed pattern); the 2026-11-06 audit says the upload needs Jamin in person with his Apple ID; AMD starts 2027-05-03.
cost: A broken app on a new iOS version, or a blocked update, with days of delay while Jamin is unavailable; every delay is lost subscribers.
detect: Apple developer news emails and TestFlight on a beta iOS (assumed); nothing watches this
response: 1. Aurik is given an App Store Connect role that can upload builds. 2. Keep Xcode current on the Mac. 3. Each September, install the new iOS on a test phone and run the scan flow.
smallest_fix: Check whether Aurik has an App Store Connect user with a role that allows uploads and release, write the build-and-upload steps so he can follow them, and note the April and September checks on Jamin's calendar.
sources: https://www.developer.apple.com/news/upcoming-requirements/ (search snippet, page not read in full) ; docs/launch-gaps-2026-11-06.md:107-110 ; native/README.md:19-24 ; docs/readiness/BRIEF.md (AMD start date)

event: A subscriber cancels or gets a refund and keeps Plus longer than they should, because RevenueCat is not told about it by Apple until the phone syncs.
trigger: RevenueCat says App Store server notifications are not needed for most subscription updates, but without them a refund 'might only appear after the Customer opens the app again'; Pexi's server asks RevenueCat on demand with a 10-minute memory.
cost: Tiny: a few days of Plus on a refunded subscription; the real risk is the reverse (a paying user shown as free, see item 5).
detect: nothing detects it; the cost is too small to alarm
response: 1. In the RevenueCat dashboard use the Apple server-notification setup button. 2. Check that notifications arrive. 3. Otherwise accept the lag.
smallest_fix: Either press RevenueCat's button to set up the Apple notification URL (5 minutes) or write down that the small lag is accepted. Not worth more.
sources: https://www.revenuecat.com/docs/platform-resources/server-notifications/apple-server-notifications (search summary; page not read in full) ; app/src/scan-quota.ts:49-51

event: A release build is made with the wrong RevenueCat key, or the key setup is missing, and purchases fail for real shoppers or in Apple review.
trigger: RevenueCat's launch checklist says never submit an app with a Test Store key; Pexi's key sync refuses a secret key (sk_...) but accepts any other text, so a test or empty key would pass; an empty key shows no plans.
cost: A rejection under 2.1 (in-app purchase not working) or a live paywall with no prices; a day or more per cycle.
detect: The build step does not check the prefix; the Apple reviewer or a shopper would find out
response: 1. Check the key in the build is the real iOS public key. 2. Rebuild and re-upload. 3. Reply to Apple with the fixed build.
smallest_fix: Make the key sync refuse an iOS release build unless the key starts with appl_ (and is non-empty), and add the sandbox purchase test (Aurik's item 7) to the release checklist.
sources: native/scripts/sync-web.mjs:55-65 ; native/config/revenuecat.config.example.json ; https://www.revenuecat.com/docs/test-and-launch/launch-checklist (item 13) ; https://developer.apple.com/app-store/review/guidelines/ (2.1(b))

event: Launch day: Jamin releases the app and starts promoting it at once, but in-app purchases do not work yet or a bad update reaches everyone before anyone can stop it.
trigger: RevenueCat says the app must be released before purchases work in production and advises waiting up to 24 hours before marketing and using a phased release; Pexi chose manual release (NOW.md:93) and nothing about phasing or the wait was found.
cost: Early shoppers meet a paywall that cannot buy (a 1-star and a missed first subscriber); a bad build to 100 percent of users instead of a slice.
detect: Aurik or Jamin trying a purchase after release; no checklist step found
response: 1. After release, wait for 'Cleared for Sale' then up to 24 hours before announcing. 2. Use phased release for each update and halt it on a bad sign. 3. Do a real purchase check on release day.
smallest_fix: Put three lines in the release checklist: manual release, wait up to 24 hours before announcing, phased release on for updates.
sources: https://www.revenuecat.com/docs/test-and-launch/launch-checklist (first release, items 16 and 17) ; NOW.md:93 ; app/public/js/screens/paywall.js:114 (paywall says so when no price can be drawn)

event: A key has to be rotated (laptop theft, a leaked key, a provider request) and the rotation silently breaks something, most likely Plus checks or Claude estimates.
trigger: The breach plan lists the keys and says to rotate them, but a rotation has never been done; a wrong RevenueCat key causes a silent free-tier downgrade (item 5); the Claude estimate path has its own key and cap.
cost: A breach response that itself causes an outage; hours of confusion during an already bad day.
detect: A failed rotation would not show up in the alarm for the RevenueCat case
response: 1. Rotate one key at a time. 2. After each, run the probe and a Plus sandbox check. 3. Record the date.
response_exists: yes: docs/privacy/breach-plan.md:41-53 lists the keys and rotation steps
smallest_fix: Do one dry-run rotation of the Anthropic key and the RevenueCat secret key on a quiet day with the check from item 5, and add the post-rotation checks to the breach plan.
sources: docs/privacy/breach-plan.md:19,41-53 ; app/src/scan-quota.ts:205-218

event: The Claude model Pexi uses for price estimates is retired or its settings are refused, and estimates quietly stop.
trigger: The estimate path uses a fixed model id in code (claude-haiku-4-5-20251001); Anthropic's own page lists its 'tentative retirement date' as not sooner than 2026-10-15 (already passed) and promises at least 60 days' email notice; retired models fail, and the API removes some sampling settings in the 2026-10-21 version.
cost: No estimates for shoppers who agreed to them (a core promise when Pexi has no price); fix needs a code change and deploy; the call count and cap alerts watch volume, not failure.
detect: A notice email to the Anthropic account holder (assumed); the estimate failure itself is not alarmed (assumed from the cap-only alert in the brief)
response: 1. Read the deprecation notice and pick the replacement model named there. 2. Change the model id, run the tests, deploy. 3. Check one estimate on the live server.
smallest_fix: Confirm who receives Anthropic's notices, make the model id a server setting so a swap does not need a code change, and add a monthly look at the deprecation page on Jamin's calendar.
sources: identify/src/range-ask.ts:213 ; app/server.ts:1582 ; identify/src/describe.ts:87 ; https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/model-deprecations

event: Open Food Facts or the public Overpass server starts refusing or banning Pexi's server because all lookups come from one home IP, and barcode misses or store lookups fail.
trigger: OFF's published limit is 15 product reads a minute per IP with a ban possible, and it asks every app for a named User-Agent; Pexi's live OFF call sends none, and a failed call is retried on the next scan; the Overpass call still says 'shin-beta ... six testers' and the Overpass wiki says commercial use should use self-hosted or paid servers and stay under 10,000 queries a day.
cost: Barcode misses with no name and no store info for every shopper at once, during a viral spike; an IP ban lasts until OFF is emailed. Operational only, no licence opinion.
detect: OFF failures appear in scan logs as 'off_failed' (checked in code) but nothing alarms on a rising rate
response: 1. If OFF or Overpass answer 429 or 503, pause that source (the server already tolerates a miss) and wait. 2. Email OFF to explain if banned. 3. Add the proper User-Agent and a per-minute ceiling.
smallest_fix: Send a named User-Agent with contact on both calls (update the stale Overpass one), cap OFF at about 10 a minute with a short pause on 429 or 503, and add the failure rate to the alarm.
sources: app/src/open-food-facts.ts:112-125 ; app/src/stores.ts:308-318 ; https://openfoodfacts.github.io/openfoodfacts-server/api/ ; https://wiki.openstreetmap.org/wiki/Overpass_API

event: A burst of new Plus subscribers or scans pushes past the server's own ceiling of 120 RevenueCat lookups a minute and new paying devices are treated as free until it eases.
trigger: Over the ceiling the server answers 'not Plus' for any device with no remembered answer and only prints one log line a minute; with a 10-minute memory, roughly 1,200 active paying devices is the steady limit (calculated, not load tested).
cost: At a viral peak, new subscribers pay and see the free cap; refunds and bad reviews exactly when attention is highest. Not live until limits are on.
detect: One warning line in the server log; no alarm
response: 1. Check the log for the limit warning. 2. Raise the ceiling or the memory time if RevenueCat's own limits allow. 3. Restart changes nothing; it clears the memory.
smallest_fix: Make the over-ceiling case say 'Plus' for a device that RevenueCat has ever answered Plus for, and count over-ceiling events into the alarm; check RevenueCat's published rate limit before raising it.
sources: app/src/scan-quota.ts:48-51,196-203
